```{r}
source("setup.R")
```

```{r}

# Age
age_plot <- ggplot(
  stupiddf3,
  aes(x = Age)
) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 3,
    fill = "#8B5CF6",
    color = "white",
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(15, 95, by = 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Age Distribution of Users",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_site() +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10)
  )

# Gender
gender_df <- stupiddf3 %>%
  count(Gender) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = n / sum(n) * 100
  )

gender_plot <- ggplot(
  gender_df,
  aes(
    x = Gender,
    y = percent,
    fill = Gender
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.7,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", percent)),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gender of Users",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percent"
  ) +
  theme_site() +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10)
  )

# Income
incomedf <- stupiddf3 %>%
  count(Income)

incomedf$Income[is.na(incomedf$Income)] <- "No Response"

incomedf <- incomedf %>%
  mutate(
    percent = n / sum(n) * 100,
    Income = factor(
      Income,
      levels = c(
        "No Response",
        "Studying",
        "$/ 00-20k",
        "$/ 20-40k",
        "$/ 40-60k",
        "$/ 60-80k",
        "$/ 80-100k",
        "$/100-120k",
        "> $/120k"
      )
    )
  )

income_plot <- ggplot(
  incomedf,
  aes(
    x = Income,
    y = percent,
    fill = percent
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.72,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", percent)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#E9D5FF",
    high = "#8B5CF6"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.20))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Income Distribution",
    subtitle = "Percentage of Users by Income Category",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percent"
  ) +
  theme_site() +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10)
  )

# Educataion
educdf <- stupiddf3 %>%
  count(EducationLevel)

educdf$EducationLevel[is.na(educdf$EducationLevel)] <- "No Response"

educdf <- educdf %>%
  mutate(
    percent = n / sum(n) * 100,
    EducationLevel = factor(
      EducationLevel,
      levels = c(
        "No Response",
        "Diploma Level",
        "High School",
        "Bachelor Degree",
        "Masters Degree",
        "Doctorate",
        "College Degree"
      )
    )
  )

education_plot <- ggplot(
  educdf,
  aes(
    x = EducationLevel,
    y = percent,
    fill = percent
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.72,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", percent)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#CCFBF1",
    high = "#14B8A6"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.20))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Education Level Distribution",
    subtitle = "Percentage of Users by Education Level",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percent"
  ) +
  theme_site() +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10)
  )
```
